lubricantEye.use: Used to relieve dry, gritty or tired eyes.
warnings: Do not touch the dropper tip to the eye.
Discard after opening as per label (often 28 days).
Refer a painful red eye, light sensitivity or reduced vision urgently.

earWax.use: Used to soften and help remove ear wax.
warnings: Do not use if the eardrum may be perforated, or with ear pain, discharge or dizziness.
Do not insert cotton buds into the ear canal.

folic.use: Commonly recommended before conception and in early pregnancy to reduce the risk of neural tube defects.
warnings: Higher doses are used only on medical advice.
Speak to a doctor/midwife about pregnancy supplements.

vitD.use: Supports calcium absorption and bone health; used for dietary supplementation.
warnings: Do not exceed the labelled dose; high doses only on medical advice.

calciumD.use: Used as a dietary supplement for calcium and vitamin D.
warnings: Separate from some antibiotics (e.g., ciprofloxacin, tetracyclines) and thyroid tablets.
May cause constipation.

iron.use: Used as an iron supplement; iron-deficiency should be confirmed by a doctor.
warnings: May cause dark stools, constipation or stomach upset.
Accidental iron overdose is dangerous for children — store securely.
Separate from antacids, calcium and tea/coffee.

multivit.use: Used to supplement the diet; not a substitute for a balanced diet.
warnings: Do not combine multiple vitamin products without advice.
Contains iron — keep away from children.

vitC.use: Used as a dietary supplement of vitamin C.
warnings: High doses may cause stomach upset.
Caution with history of kidney stones.

omega3.use: Used as a dietary supplement of omega-3 fatty acids.
warnings: Check with a doctor if taking anticoagulants.
May cause fishy aftertaste.

probiotic.use: Used as a dietary supplement of live bacteria.
warnings: Not a replacement for ORS in diarrhoea.
Seek advice if immunocompromised.

glucose.use: Used as a quick source of glucose, e.g., for treating mild low blood sugar in people with diabetes.
warnings: Severe hypoglycaemia (confusion, unconsciousness) is an emergency.
People with diabetes should follow their care plan.

bcomplexTonic.use: Used as a dietary supplement of B vitamins. Does not treat any disease.
warnings: Contains sugar — diabetics check label.
Not a substitute for a balanced diet.

ironTonic.generic: Ferric ammonium citrate + Folic acid + Vitamin B12 syrup
ironTonic.use: Used as an iron and vitamin dietary supplement.
warnings: May darken stools or stain teeth — use a straw/rinse mouth.
Keep away from children (iron).

calciumTonic.use: Used as a calcium and vitamin D dietary supplement.
warnings: Separate from certain antibiotics and thyroid tablets.
Shake well.

kidsMultiTonic.use: Used as a vitamin supplement for children as per label age.
warnings: Use the measuring cup provided; do not exceed dose.
Contains sugar.

thermometer.use: Used to measure body temperature (oral, underarm or rectal as per instructions).
warnings: Clean the tip before and after use.
Fever is commonly defined as 38 °C (100.4 °F) or higher.

irThermo.use: Used for non-contact screening of body temperature.
warnings: Follow distance instructions.
Confirm unusual readings with a contact thermometer.

bpArm.use: Used to measure blood pressure and pulse at home.
warnings: Rest 5 minutes seated, back supported, arm at heart level, correct cuff size.
Avoid caffeine/exercise 30 minutes before measuring.
Share readings with your doctor; do not change medicines yourself.

bpWrist.use: Used to measure blood pressure at the wrist.
warnings: Keep the wrist at heart level during measurement.
Upper-arm monitors are generally preferred for accuracy.

glucometer.use: Used by people with diabetes to monitor blood glucose levels.
warnings: Use only compatible test strips.
Wash and dry hands before testing.
Follow your diabetes team's targets.

strips.use: Used with a compatible glucose meter to test blood sugar.
warnings: Keep in the original vial, tightly closed, away from heat and moisture.
Do not use after expiry or beyond the opened-vial life on the label.

lancets.use: Used with a lancing device to obtain a small blood sample.
warnings: Single use only — never share.
Dispose of in a sharps container.

oximeter.use: Used to estimate blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂) and pulse rate.
warnings: Nail polish, cold fingers and movement can affect readings.
Seek urgent care for breathlessness regardless of the reading.

nebulizer.use: Used to deliver prescribed inhaled medicines as a mist.
warnings: Use only with medicines prescribed for nebulisation.
Clean and dry parts after each use.

spacer.use: Used with a pressurised metered-dose inhaler to improve delivery of medicine to the lungs.
warnings: Wash as per instructions and air-dry.
Check compatibility with the inhaler.

sanitizer.use: Used to reduce germs on hands when soap and water are not available.
warnings: Flammable.
Not effective on visibly dirty hands — wash with soap and water.
Supervise children.

mask.use: Used to reduce spread of respiratory droplets.
warnings: Single use; replace when damp.
Cover nose and mouth fully.

toothpaste.use: Used for daily oral care and relief of tooth sensitivity.
warnings: Persistent tooth pain needs a dentist.
Supervise children to avoid swallowing.

lipBalm.use: Used to moisturise and protect dry, chapped lips.
warnings: For external use only.
Change regularly (every 4–6 hours).

zincOxide.use: Used to protect skin and soothe mild nappy rash.
warnings: Change nappies frequently and allow nappy-free time.
Seek advice if rash is severe, blistered, spreading or with fever.
Choose the correct size by weight.

babyWipes.use: Used for gentle cleansing during nappy changes.
warnings: Discontinue if irritation occurs.

babyLotion.use: Used to moisturise a baby's skin.
warnings: Patch test; stop if irritation occurs.

amoxicillin.use: Prescription antibiotic for certain bacterial infections. Not effective against viruses (e.g., common cold).
warnings: Do not use with penicillin allergy.
Complete the course as prescribed.
May cause diarrhoea or rash.

coamox.use: Prescription antibiotic for certain bacterial infections.
warnings: Do not use with penicillin allergy.
Take with a meal.
Complete the course.

azithromycin.use: Prescription antibiotic for certain bacterial infections.
warnings: Take exactly as prescribed.
May interact with some heart-rhythm medicines.

ciprofloxacin.use: Prescription antibiotic for certain bacterial infections.
warnings: Separate from antacids, calcium, iron and zinc (reduced absorption).
Tendon pain — stop and seek advice.
May cause photosensitivity.

metronidazole.use: Prescription medicine for certain bacterial and protozoal infections.
warnings: Avoid alcohol during treatment and for at least 48 hours after (risk of severe reaction).
May cause metallic taste.

metformin.use: Prescription medicine used in type 2 diabetes to help control blood glucose.
warnings: Take with meals to reduce stomach upset.
Dose depends on kidney function.
Follow the prescriber's plan; do not stop suddenly without advice.

glimepiride.use: Prescription medicine used in type 2 diabetes.
warnings: Can cause low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) — do not skip meals.
Know the signs: sweating, shaking, confusion.

amlodipine.use: Prescription medicine used for high blood pressure and angina.
warnings: May cause ankle swelling, flushing or headache.
Do not stop without medical advice.

losartan.use: Prescription medicine used for high blood pressure.
warnings: Not used in pregnancy.
Monitoring of kidney function and potassium may be needed.
NSAIDs may reduce effect and affect kidneys.

atorvastatin.use: Prescription medicine used to lower cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.
warnings: Report unexplained muscle pain or weakness.
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice.
Not used in pregnancy.
